This hint contains the essential information about gameplay, the map, and raids. 
 
Raids. 
The add-on’s core mechanic is its raid system. You cannot leave the Radar shelter in the usual way. Instead, choose tasks in the notebook, then select a location on the map to travel to. Each location has a rank. There are four ranks: first, second, third, and Darkness, each marked with a different color on the map.
A raid lasts 40 minutes. Any transition from a raid location takes you back to the shelter and consumes in-game time. You can extend raid duration by upgrading the shelter. When the timer expires, your character becomes “lost”: the chance of returning to the shelter alive is only 10%. Upgrade your PDA to improve your survival chance: level 2 gives +10%, and level 3 gives +20%. The Informant provides information about safe paths: +10%. The “Block-Six” anabiotic from the notebook’s special equipment adds another 20%. 

Random events. 
The add-on has a random event system called “rumors.” Information about each location circulates over the stalker radio, but it may be false. Conditions at locations change every 3 hours. If needed, you can buy current intelligence about a location from the Informant. Event danger depends on the location’s rank: the farther north you go, the more dangerous the events become. Choose tasks carefully; nobody pays extra for difficult conditions during a raid. Sometimes it is better to wait in the shelter for more favorable conditions. 

Death. 
You can die during a raid. If you do, all equipment in your inventory is lost, and tasks at that location count as failed, with all the consequences that entails. Death removes a configurable percentage of your rank (set this in the MCM menu); your money is retained. The higher the protagonist’s rank, the more dangerous and better-paid tasks clients offer. Rank increases by completing tasks and through certain activity during a raid. Saving during a raid is disabled for a better gameplay experience and for technical reasons. The game saves automatically when you return to the shelter after a raid. Do not fear death: the mod’s economy and gameplay are designed with this outcome in mind. Keep several equipment sets ready, learn from your mistakes, and do not carry all available medicine and food. Run if the situation calls for it. Gameplay differs greatly from the usual F5/F9. Plan your survival strategy and improvise: that is how you can reach the Legend of the Zone rank. 

Emissions. 
During a raid, you may be caught in a “surge”: a short emission lasting 3–7 minutes. Remember, you are not the only one who needs shelter; enemies will fight to the death for it. The standard anabiotic can help you survive an emission in the open without shelter. You can also sleep through the emission in the shelter, guaranteeing that no emission will occur during your next raids. 

Good luck, stalker.

Code: Syndicate-Alpha, channel 4.
From: Lyutyi, squad leader.
To: Coordinator.
Subject: Report on the AER asset. Personnel losses.
 
Hey, Central. Facts only, no whining.
First, you drove us like stray dogs. We chased those army greenhorns through the middle of nowhere for three days. Our feet were worn to the bone, gear caked in mud, guns full of sand. We lived on field rations washed down with rainwater. We wiped out the soldiers, just as agreed, but the boys were completely spent. We kept going on stimulants and pills.
Then, instead of a base and some rest, your order came in: “Make a dash to the eggheads and grab the AER prototype.” Brilliant plan. As reliable as a Swiss watch, I'd say.
We reached the site. Turns out the eggheads weren't fools and had hired proper security. A hell of a firefight broke out. We were tired, hungry, and filthy. Then our guy Bukka lost his nerve. Lack of sleep and the pressure had his eyes bulging, yeah. So he decided to play it safe. The idiot couldn't think of anything better than firing a grenade from his launcher straight into the field at the scientists. There was a crate full of pieces of that device; it went off in a storm of lightning. Half the scientists were blown to atoms, while the rest just stood there in shock. Bukka really let that VOG fly, all right. The prototype blew to pieces, damn it. Nothing but smoking scrap was left.
 
Bukka got his payback for that stunt right away: a round caught him under the armor, in the left armpit. He coughed blood for a little while; there was no point bandaging him. He wandered around for a bit, then quietly checked out. May the concrete lie heavy on him.
As for the installation itself, it was done for. After we cleared the remaining guards, we dug through the smoking wreckage and found a case with papers. The folder inside had somehow survived. It was called “AER Prototype 2.5 Calibration Report.” At least something came of this shit.
Taking that paperwork back to base through the cordons in our state would have been suicide. We pulled back to the Agroprom underground, stash number four. Word came that the fourth stash had been exposed, so we left the documents by the treatment plant—where the old rusty valves are, with rotten pipes and slime on the walls, on the lower level. The folder is packed in a sealed container.
What's left of my boys are heading underground to recover. I'm waiting for payment for the dead army men to hit our account. We'll figure out what to do with this damn calibration report later; I reckon the eggheads will pay well for it. Lyutyi, signing off.

This hint contains essential information about the notebook and trading. 
 
“Tasks” tab: 
It displays a list of tasks with the client, your reputation with them, a brief mission description, and the rewards. Hover over the “Details” button for more information; there is also an “In case of failure” window. Failing a task is expected to cost you reputation with that client. Some tasks come from unknown clients: they pay quite generously, but other clients will not approve of that work.
Each task has a deadline and a rank. The timer starts as soon as you accept the task in the notebook. Urgent tasks are best completed on your next raid; you can do the others later. Do not wait: once the timer expires, the task counts as failed. Try not to take higher-rank tasks unless you are confident you can succeed. You can take the risk, though: rank 3 tasks are sometimes available from the very beginning.
In the upper-right corner of the tasks section, you can contact the Informant. For an extra fee, the Informant can find a wider selection of tasks for you. Tasks refresh every 24 hours, at 4 a.m. 
 
“Special Equipment” tab: 
Use this tab to order special equipment. It is extremely expensive, but has unique properties that were previously unavailable. This equipment can turn even the most difficult situation in your favor. Read its description carefully and use it wisely. Remember: nothing is worth more than your life. 
 
“Shelter Upgrades” tab: 
As the name suggests, this interface lets you upgrade your shelter. Study the upgrades carefully; some provide unique capabilities for operations under the Zone’s changed conditions. 
 
Trading: 
Each client has their own stock. Shustry brings equipment to your shelter in an APC. Talk to him to choose from the stock. As your reputation grows, each client gives you discounts on the equipment they specialize in. Here is a brief summary. 
 
Summary: 
Sidorovich: shotguns, pistols, food, devices, and medium and light suits.
Barman: assault rifles, shotguns, and heavy and medium suits.
Skinflint: assault rifles, sniper rifles, and heavy and medium suits.
Hermann: pistols, submachine guns, medicine, devices, and scientist suits.
Other clients: sniper rifles, assault rifles, shotguns, submachine guns, pistols, and medium suits.
Shustry: specializes in weapon attachments and some special models.
